title: Fissile batch priming scratchpad — short-run stress and warmup artifacts
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploration of very short-run (30s-5m) stress windows to observe how small-batch priming/eviction behavior affects p95/p99 under realistic arrival jitter. Goal is to capture the transient window where KV cache + micro-batching transitions from cold->warm under bursty arrivals, and to sketch mitigations.

Experimental context (infra):
- cluster: dedicated-ci-a100-1 (single A100-40GB), baseline image: rw-runtime:canary-2025-01
- model: rw-13b-v1 (fp16) and rw-13b-q4 (int8-ish), serving runtime configured with continuous-batcher v2
- client: synthetic harness (python) generating Poisson+burst superposition arrivals; client reports exact timestamps

Input distribution and run config (short runs):
- seq len (tokens): 32 typical, 128 tail samples (5%)
- arrival profiles:
  - baseline steady: 50 qps constant for 5m
  - nano-burst: baseline 20 qps + a 10s spike to 600 qps starting at t=15s (repeats every 60s)
  - clustered: 3x bursts of 30s at 300 qps spaced by 90s
- concurrency per client: 50 (to hit runtime queueing, not client-side limits)
- batcher settings: target_batch_size: 8, max_wait_ms: 12, adaptive_timeout: on/off toggles
- cache: KV cache enabled, capacity 1.2M keys, eviction LRU, prewarm disabled

Measurements collected: qps (ingress/egress), p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (tail includes server side only), batch size distribution, kvcache hit rate, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, scheduling preemption counts, CPU steal (container-level)

Key runs and observations:
1) Baseline steady (50 qps) — 3 minutes
- model rw-13b-v1 fp16
- avg batch size: 6.9 (close to target)
- kvcache hit rate: 84% after 60s
- p50/p95/p99: 18ms / 46ms / 110ms
- GPU util: 48%
Quick note: warm convergence happens ~40s; after that stable. No significant scheduling stalls.

2) Nano-burst (10s spike to 600 qps at t=15s) — repeated every 60s, run 6 cycles
- immediate effect: batcher saturates; observed maximal batch size capped at 32 due to internal batching window cascade
- cache hit: drops temporarily from 82% -> 38% during spike (cold evictions + KV miss storm)
- tail amplification: p95 jumps from 46ms -> 720ms, p99 observed as high as 2.1s for some requests in first 5s after burst onset
- average tokens/sec increases but GPU queuing leads to request queueing; observed 12% preemption due to scheduler throttles in the VM image
- adaptive_timeout on (default) helped reduce sustained p99 after ~12s, bringing p99 back to ~260ms once cache recovered
Insight: short spikes hit both the batcher and cache simultaneously, producing multiplicative tail effects.

3) Clustered longer bursts (30s @ 300 qps)
- more pronounced steady-state resource contention; batcher oscillates between small and large batches causing jitter
- cache hit rate stays mid (58%) during bursts due to enough repeated contexts, but warmup phase still costs ~7-12s each burst
- p99 sustained ~420-650ms for duration of burst; overall throughput drop ~12% relative to baseline due to queueing timeouts and small eviction churn

4) Contrasting rw-13b-q4 (quantized) runs
- q4 reduces per-token latency ~30-40% for heavy batches; during spikes, GPU util reaches 82% vs 48% for fp16
- however cache eviction behavior similar (cache is model-agnostic); p99 still spikes but magnitude reduced (max observed 1.1s)
- tradeoff: lower per-token GPU work but more throttle on scheduler due to CPU-side serialization in quantized path (observed small CPU-bound serialization at token merge stage)

Micro-observations (funny/ugly):
- we saw a microburst pattern where batcher windowing produced 2-phase latency: immediate small batches served very quickly, then a second large batched wave (batch size 28-32) that created the long tail. This pattern repeats as queues refill.
- cleanup cron inside image evicted low-priority cache entries at t=22s in one run (investigate image housekeeping drift)
- enabling a soft-priority lane (client tagging) reduced p99 for high-priority requests by ~60% in runs where we simulated mixed priority traffic

Hypotheses to validate next:
- prefill: priming a small set of common prompts (pre-warm keys) before anticipating bursts will collapse the early 5-12s penalty. Test with prefill size 500 keys, injected 30s before a scheduled burst.
- batcher jitter smoothing: increase max_wait_ms from 12 -> 18 to allow more aggregation during spikes (trade latency for p99 reduction).
- eviction tuning: bump KV cache capacity logical threshold or change eviction to frequency-aware (LFU-ish) to reduce churn on short repeated bursts.
- adaptive hot cache replication: shadow-replicate top-100 keys across hot pool to avoid eviction thrash during short spikes.

Planned quick experiments (one-liners):
- Prewarm 500 keys + nano-burst x6, measure p99 first 20s of each burst.
- max_wait_ms=18 vs 12 vs 24 under clustered bursts; track batch size CDF and p95/p99.
- soft-priority lane enabled: mark 10% of requests high-priority during bursts; measure separation.
- small-run canary for housekeeping: disable cron job in image to check if p99 improvements correlate.

Results sketch (expected thresholds for "good enough"):
- objective: keep p99 < 300ms for 95% of bursts after first 5s.
- acceptable trade: p95 < 200ms, p50 < 40ms during steady-state.

Quick conclusions so far:
- Short bursts are dominated by multiplicative interaction between batcher windowing and KV cache misses.
- Quantized model variants reduce absolute latency but do not eliminate cache-induced tail amplification.
- Mitigations: prefill + soft-priority + slight max_wait increase seem promising; next step is a combinatorial sweep but limited to 2 variables at once.

Notes-to-self / operational runbook additions:
- add instrumentation to record batch composition per-request (which keys saturated the batch) and tag spikes with host housekeeping events
- add a canary that pre-populates top-1k keys every 3m for dedicated fleets with scheduled traffic surges
- file an infra bug for unexpected cron eviction (link REDW-4123)

Next actions (owner tagged):
- Reena: schedule 3 x 5m runs for prewarm sweep (tomorrow AM)
- Diego: instrument batch tracepoints + add CSV output for batch composition
- Mira: review image cron and propose minimal-change patch to disable during tests

Random notes:
- saw one run where batch size median was 2 but mean was 18 -> high skew indicates many small real-time requests coexisting with bulk streams (adjusting target batch size alone won't fix skew)
- consider longer-lived micro-shards for KV cache affinity to reduce cross-tenant eviction in Dedicated pools

End of scratchpad. Keep ephemeral logs attached to run ids in linked_artifacts.
